articleTitle: Kolmogorov-Arnold Network for Machine Learning-based Motor Condition Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electrical, Electronics and System Engineering (ICEESE)
abstract: Minimizing downtime in industrial production processes is paramount, and swift, accurate machine fault detection is crucial in achieving this goal. Recent advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) have facilitated significant improvements in fault detection through pattern recognition and predictive analytics. Traditional machine learning models, such as the Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), have been effective but have computational complexity and interpretability limitations due to their reliance on fixed activation functions. This paper introduces the Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (KAN) as a novel approach for machine learning-based motor condition diagnosis. Unlike conventional MLPs, KAN employs learnable activation functions parameterized by splines, eliminating the need for separate weight matrices and enhancing the model’s capacity to learn complex, non-linear relationships. Our methodology involved training the KAN model on a motor current signals dataset collected from five 2-HP induction motors, each tested under five different load conditions, comprising 3,750 signals. Experimental results demonstrate that KAN outperforms traditional MLP models, achieving a validation accuracy of 88.27% compared to MLP’s 84.10%, even without hyperparameter tuning. Furthermore, KAN provides greater interpretability by converting learned splines into symbolic functions, offering a transparent understanding of the model’s decision-making process. Despite its longer training time, KAN’s enhanced accuracy and interpretability present a compelling case for its application in motor fault detection and predictive maintenance. This study underscores the potential of the KAN architecture in advancing AI-driven diagnostics in industrial settings.

articleTitle: Optimization Cooling System of Photovoltaic Thermal Collector System for Sustainable Green Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electrical, Electronics and System Engineering (ICEESE)
abstract: Solar power is considered a promising energy option to meet the growing global demand for energy and to achieve a shift to clean energy. Compared to other renewable energy sources such as radio frequency (RF), solar energy is easily accessible and has a low environmental impact. However, the surface temperature of photovoltaic (PV) panels significantly affects their power output and performance. In this project, a hybrid cooling system was designed and implemented, combining air and water cooling mechanisms. The microcontroller-based control system enables solar panels to generate more energy compared to radio energy harvesting. Air cooling is activated at 35°C, while the water pump operates above 45°C. The results revealed that the peak voltage increased from 15.08V to 16.95V, with a temperature reduction of up to 22°C. The cooled PV system achieved a maximum output power of 9.49W at midday. Moreover, this designed cooling system improved electrical efficiency by 28.37%. The automatic cooling technique effectively reduces cell temperature, enhancing electrical output and overall efficiency for sustainable green technology.

Author Keywords: hybrid air and water cooling system

articleTitle: Feature Evaluation based on Correlation Coefficient Filter Method for Electrical Motor Condition Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electrical, Electronics and System Engineering (ICEESE)
abstract: In the realm of electrical motor condition monitoring, identifying optimal features is crucial for enhancing predictive maintenance strategies. This paper focuses on analyzing features for low speed electrical motor condition monitoring, aiming to determine the optimal number of features that can be monitored with fewer sensors without significantly compromising the accuracy and precision of the predictive models. This study utilizes conventional statistical feature extraction methods, initially considering a set of 30 features derived from three sensors. Feature selection is performed using Pearson and Spearman correlation coefficient filter methods to identify the most relevant features. Subsequently, a systematic reduction of feature from thirty to three is carried out. The filtered features are then evaluated using three different machine learning models. The resultant accuracy and precision of these model are compared to assess the impact of feature reduction on model performance. The findings demonstrate that it is possible to maintain high accuracy and precision with a reduced number of features, thereby optimizing sensor usage and improving the efficiency of condition monitoring systems for electrical motors.

articleTitle: Utilization of Force Sensor and Deep Q-Learning Algorithm in Object Grasping Simulation Identified by Mask R-CNN
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electrical, Electronics and System Engineering (ICEESE)
abstract: This research focuses on the development and evaluation of a robotic grasping system that combines a force sensor and a Deep Q-Learning algorithm, with objects identified using Mask R-CNN. The system’s performance was tested using 10 randomly selected objects with varying shapes, sizes, and hardness to assess its adaptability to different scenarios. During training, the Deep Q-Learning network was trained over 1000 episodes, showing stable convergence with increasing average reward values per episode. The Random method demonstrated a grasp success rate of 62% and action efficiency of 60%, while the Pre-Train VPG method showed improvement with a grasp success rate of 67% and action efficiency of 65%. The VPG with Mask R-CNN further improved results, achieving a 77% grasp success rate and 76% action efficiency. Our method with binary reward achieved an 81% grasp success rate and 80% action efficiency, while our fully developed method recorded the best results with an 86% grasp success rate and 84% action efficiency. Mask R-CNN maintained an object detection accuracy of 98%, ensuring precise identification for grasping by the UR5 robotic arm. The processing time from object detection to grasp execution was 0.5 seconds per step, enabling real-time operation. The Dynpick force sensor provided accurate feedback on force and torque, allowing for adjustments with a variation of ±5% from the optimal value, crucial for maintaining the integrity of the objects tested. The findings demonstrate that the developed system is effective and efficient in handling various objects, indicating its potential for practical robotic applications. This research highlights the significant contributions of machine learning algorithms and sensors in enhancing robotic performance, paving the way for future advancements in the field.

articleTitle: Intelligent Wireless Charging Control System for E-Bikes Using Wireless Power Transfer Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electrical, Electronics and System Engineering (ICEESE)
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative intelligent charging control system designed specifically for electric bicycles (e-bikes) utilizing Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) technology. The system features transmitter and receiver coils integrated into the front tires of the e-bike and within the charging station, enabling efficient wireless charging. The core of the system is an Arduino Nano microcontroller integrated with key components such as a voltage divider circuit, an infrared sensor for e-bike detection, an HC-12 module for communication, and a solid-state relay for power supply control. The proposed system ensures both safety and efficiency in wireless charging by continuously monitoring battery voltage, initiating charging processes as necessary, and automatically discontinuing charging once the battery reaches an optimum level of 48 volts. Selected results from experimental tests are presented to verify the effectiveness and reliability of the proposed system. This intelligent system promotes responsible charging practices and enhances user convenience, contributing significantly to the advancement of a greener and more sustainable electric mobility ecosystem.

articleTitle: Evaluating Axle and Leaf Spring Sensor Setup Methods for Weight Sensing on Lorry
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electrical, Electronics and System Engineering (ICEESE)
abstract: This study investigates the optimal configuration of sensors for lorry weight sensing undertaking a comparative study of strain gauge setups on the lorry axle and leaf spring respectively to provide comparative insights on sensor setup not done in previous research. These sensors were strategically attached on axles and leaf spring. Two setups were studied namely setup of strain gauges at front axle and setup of strain gauges at leaf spring. Signals from these sensors were processed by signal conditioning circuit to produce output in voltages that represent the weight being measured. Load tests were conducted, and the output voltages tabulated. The data was analyzed to look for linear and accurate measurements using linear regression. The coefficient of determination R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, standard error (SE) and sum square error (SS) from ANOVA were analyzed to seek the closest approximation to true weight. Based on the results, it is determined that placing the strain gauge at the front axle produced the most linear and accurate measurements among the two setups. This may imply that attaching strain gauge to axle may provide more reliable strain measurements for weight sensing.

articleTitle: Predictive Modeling of Monthly Wind Energy Production in Thailand Using Machine Learning Approaches
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electrical, Electronics and System Engineering (ICEESE)
abstract: This study presents a predictive modeling approach for estimating monthly wind production in Thailand using advanced machine learning methodologies. Logistic Regression (LR), Extreme Learning Machines (ELM), and Support Vector Regression (SVR) were employed and evaluated through 5-fold and 10-fold cross-validation techniques. The dataset spans from 2018 to 2023, obtained from the Thai Meteorological Department and Department of Alternative Energy Development and Efficiency, encompassing monthly wind production data. Performance metrics including Mean Squared Error (MSE) and Mean Absolute Error (MAE) were used to assess model accuracy. Results indicate that SVR consistently outperforms LR and ELM in terms of predictive accuracy, demonstrating lower MSE and MAE values during both training and testing phases. Specifically, during the testing phase of the 10-fold cross-validation, the model achieved an MSE of 67.3646 and an MAE of 6.5194. This study contributes to the advancement of predictive modeling in renewable energy forecasting and provides valuable insights for policymakers and stakeholders in Thailand’s energy sector.

articleTitle: On-board Truck Weight Sensing System based on Current Loop Transmission
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electrical, Electronics and System Engineering (ICEESE)
abstract: On-board truck weight sensing is essential to monitor truck loads and avoid overloading. Challenges faced in current works include addressing noise generated in the system. Hence, this work aims to develop truck weighing system using the 4–20 mA current loop transmission, with a specific emphasis on developing an effective weighing system for the truck front axle. Firstly, a signal conditioning circuit was developed to amplify and filter noise in the electrical signal obtained from the weight sensor. The electrical signals from the signal conditioning were transmitted to the dashboard for processing using the 4–20 mA current loop transmission method. On the dashboard, the current signals were converted to voltage signals and digitally processed by an Arduino microcontroller to calculate and display the corresponding weight at the LCD display. The 4–20 mA current transmission produces stable readings with less drifts. The weight measurements were successfully implemented for the front axle using human loads producing acceptable error. The findings highlight the advancement in signal conditioning and transmission techniques for addressing challenges in real-world field conditions for on-board truck weight sensing.

articleTitle: IoT based Monitoring and Investigation of the Effect of Water Level, Temperature and humidity to the Hydroponic based plant
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electrical, Electronics and System Engineering (ICEESE)
abstract: Hydroponic plant system cultivate different plants without utilizing the soil. The purpose of the paper is to monitor and analyze the parameters of hydroponic system sensors which include Water Level Sensor, pH water level sensor, and DHT11 (Humidity and Temperature sensor). This sensor will monitor the water supply level, humidity, and temperature of the plant, and also pH water level. Moreover, to make this hydroponic plant into ‘Smart Hydroponic Plant System’ is we implement a low-cost, low-power system on a chip microcontroller with integrated Wi-Fi and dual-mode Bluetooth called as ESP32 to control the pump. The pump will draw water from a tank connected. This component will able farmer to monitor their plant through their computer. In another words, the ESP32 is a bridge for the hardware or plant to communicate with device such as smartphones.

articleTitle: Mitigation of Third Harmonic Current at the Generator Neutral using Selective Hybrid Grounding
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electrical, Electronics and System Engineering (ICEESE)
abstract: This paper proposed a selective hybrid grounding to mitigate the high third harmonic (TH) current in generator neutral mainly due to triplen harmonic. In a medium voltage network, neutral earth resistance (NER) grounding method is commonly used to limit the fault current rating in the generator neutral. Due to triplen harmonic at generator neutral, NER has experienced overheating over prolonged periods during normal operating conditions. This paper explores the hybrid grounding solution utilizing the existing NER combined with grounding transformer to provide TH current mitigation and limiting fault current. It is a hybrid method that can selectively combine the low resistance and high resistance grounding. In this paper, investigation on the proposed selective hybrid method is presented. In this method, a high resistance, R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">harmonic</inf> is imposed on the generator neutral during the normal condition and a low resistance, R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sec</inf>, is imposed during the phase-to-ground fault. The two secondary resistors are connected to the generator neutral via grounding transformer and equipped with switching capability. The simulation was carried out on the simplified system network of Universiti Teknologi Petronas (UTP) using real parameters. Characteristics of voltage and current for the switching condition was analyzed and the optimum value of secondary resistance is also explored. It is found that the hybrid method able to mitigate third harmonic current in neutral during normal condition and maintain a safe fault current level.

articleTitle: Major Depressive Disorder Detection using Effective Connectivity of Resting-state EEG Signals and 2D-Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electrical, Electronics and System Engineering (ICEESE)
abstract: Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) is a common mental health condition that can have a significant impact on an individual’s quality of life. This study is focused on the detection of MDD from resting-state Electroencephalogram (EEG) signals, using Effective Connectivity (EC) and 2D-Convolutional Neural Network (2D-CNN). MDD is a common mental health condition that is difficult to diagnose accurately through clinical assessment and self-reported symptoms. The clinical assessment and self-reported symptoms differ differently, and individuals may not always accurately report their experience due to various factors and thus, lead to inconsistencies in diagnosing MDD. The aim of this study is to explore the use of EC and 2D-CNN to overcome the challenges of utilizing complex characteristics of EEG signals for detection of MDD. A dataset of EEG recordings from 30 individuals with MDD and 30 HC, is used for this study. Overall, this study highlights the potential of EC and 2D-CNNs as a powerful tool for the analysis of complex EEG data and the detection of MDD. The results show that the proposed MDD diagnosis algorithm achieved 98.24% and 98.07% for sample-based and subject-based respectively in classifying MDD and HC test subjects.

articleTitle: Data Analysis of Sensors Value Using Various Moving Average Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electrical, Electronics and System Engineering (ICEESE)
abstract: Sensors such as force and distance sensors are crucial for accurate measurements in many engineering applications. However, sensor data often contains noise that can compromise the reliability of the measurements. This study addresses the problem of noisy sensor data by applying several moving average methods to smooth the data. The methods investigated include simple, exponential, modified, square-root, and triangular moving averages, implemented using MATLAB. The effectiveness of these methods is evaluated using the Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) as a performance metric. The results demonstrate that all moving average methods significantly reduce noise, with the exponential moving average showing the lowest RMSE values, thereby indicating superior performance in improving data quality.

articleTitle: Secure Communications Employing Intelligent Reflecting Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electrical, Electronics and System Engineering (ICEESE)
abstract: This paper focuses on secure transmission with multiple intelligent reflecting surfaces (IRS) for millimeter-wave (mmWave) and terahertz (THz) systems. Specifically, it explores the scenario where a base station (BS) and a user (D) utilize multi-IRS for transmission while having active eavesdropping from an eavesdropper (E). There is no direct path between the BS and the user, nor between the eavesdropper and BS. Considering hardware implementation, the conditions for discrete phase shifts of IRS reflections are designed. Under these conditions, we maximize the system’s secrecy rate of the mmWave/THz systems. We solve the non-convex problem by decomposing it into two sub-problems: optimizing beamforming and then optimizing the reflection phase shift matrix. Then, these sub-problems are jointly optimized. For the beamforming optimization problem, we propose a closed-form optimal solution. For the optimization problem of the reflection phase shift matrix, we propose a method based on semidefinite relaxation programming (SDR) and element-wise block coordinate descent (E-BCD) to optimize the matrix. Simulation results show the effectiveness of the proposed methods.

articleTitle: Sensitivity Study of a Coplanar Waveguide Antenna-Based Sensor for Hydration Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electrical, Electronics and System Engineering (ICEESE)
abstract: This paper presents a study on a coplanar waveguide (CPW) antenna-based sensor operating at frequency of 2.4 GHz. Designed with a compact size of 30 mm × 30 mm, the antenna-based sensor utilizes filtered paper as its substrate material. The performance analysis of the CPW antenna-based sensor focuses on evaluating its sensitivity in detecting various types of sweat for hydration monitoring. The investigation encompasses a range of hydration levels, including hydrated, intermediate, dehydrated and severely dehydrated sweat. Results indicate that the CPW antenna-based sensor demonstrated high sensitivity to sweat, as evidenced by significant shifts in resonant frequency with increasing sweat volume. The maximum simulated frequency shift observed is 1.79 GHz when the CPW antenna-based sensor is fully immersed in sweat, compared to a 0.43 GHz shift at 10% immersion. The CPW antenna-based sensor effectively distinguishes between hydration states, with hydrated sweat exhibiting a substantial frequency shift of 74.21 % while dehydrated sweat showed a 45.42 % frequency shift.

articleTitle: A Decision-Support for Rubber Tree Clone Diagnosis using Fuzzy Logic
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electrical, Electronics and System Engineering (ICEESE)
abstract: Initial classification of the rubber tree clone series at the early stage is a crucial decision as there are a lot of clones that need to be chosen for plantation purposes. This research focuses on developing a decision-support for rubber tree clone diagnosis based on optical properties using Fuzzy logic. This work selected three RRIM clones: RRIM 2007, RRIM 2014, and RRIM 3001, based on the most excellent latex general remarks with good latex yielding and suitable for timber products. The total samples selected consist of 480 samples and 50 samples from each clone for the development of the system and validation, respectively. The prior researcher extracted the data using the developed optical sensor with RGB LED and simple statistical analyses to find the correlation and relationship between RGB spectrum and clone properties. The preliminary statistical data, such as information on the descriptive; box plots of the RGB spectrum, are needed to use as the membership inputs and the clone type as the outputs in the Fuzzy logic system. The decision system is a success, with findings showing that the model can adequately validate RRIM 2014 with 98% accuracy, compared to 76% and 56% for RRIM 3001 and RRIM 2007, respectively.

articleTitle: Elastic TiO2-embedded silicone oil- (poly)dimethylsiloxane membrane for compliant robotics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electrical, Electronics and System Engineering (ICEESE)
abstract: Polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) is essential in compliant robotics due to its versatility, elasticity, and biocompatible properties. Despite all the advantages, PDMS has a drawback of low dielectric permittivity, requiring high electric fields for significant actuation strains, which is the main cause leading to premature membrane breakdown. This paper investigates a dual-filler embedding approach using titanium dioxide (TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) and silicone oil (SO) to enhance the electromechanical properties and elasticity of PDMS membranes. A PDMS pre-blend was prepared by mixing commercial PDMS with a specified ratio of TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and SO, forming single-filler and dual-filler systems, followed by curing in a laboratory oven. The membranes were subsequently characterized through uniaxial tensile testing to determine tensile strength, elongation at break, and Young’s modulus. Breakdown strength analysis was conducted using a breakdown tester with step-up voltage, while relative permittivity was examined with an impedance analyzer within a frequency range of 30 MHz to 20 Hz. The dual-filler approach significantly improved tensile properties and elasticity, making PDMS membranes suitable for compliant robotics. This hybrid strategy creates a TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-embedded silicone oil-(poly)dimethylsiloxane composite membrane capable of withstanding extensive deformation thereby improving the performance and elasticity of compliant robotic systems.

articleTitle: Development and Comparative Analysis of Reduced-switch Multilevel Inverter Topology for Grid-connected Application: Asymmetric DC Source Configuration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electrical, Electronics and System Engineering (ICEESE)
abstract: Multilevel inverters (MLIs) are becoming more appealing due to their ability to produce high-quality AC output with better efficiency and reduced harmonic without the need for filter circuits. As a result, MLIs have been widely implemented in industrial applications, motor drives, renewable energy and also as grid integration inverter. However, conventional MLIs require numerous switches, leading to increase complexity, cost and higher potential of failure. Hence, a 15-level reduced-switch multilevel inverter (RSMLI) topology with an asymmetric DC source configuration is introduced in this paper. The RSMLI aims to provide an alternative for a more compact and cost-effective solution. PSIM software is used to model and analyse the circuits focusing on the influence of the number of DC sources, switches, voltage stress and circuit complexity on inverter performance. The findings indicate that a higher variety and rating of DC source can increase operating circuit stress and switch ratings, subsequently increase the inverter’s cost. Therefore, the proposed RSMLI topology mitigates these issues by utilizing less DC source variety and lower-rated switches, making it a promising alternative for various applications, especially grid-connected systems.

articleTitle: Development of a Geolocation-Based Database System for Enhanced Diabetes Management
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electrical, Electronics and System Engineering (ICEESE)
abstract: The built environment significantly influences the management and outcomes of Type 2 diabetes. Factors such as the availability of recreational areas, proximity to healthcare facilities, and access to healthy food options can impact patients’ physical activity levels and overall health. This paper addresses the challenges of collecting built environment data for Type 2 diabetes patients by utilizing the Google Maps API to save information about nearby facilities. This comprehensive data provides healthcare practitioners with a holistic view of patients’ surroundings, which is crucial for optimizing diabetes management. I have successfully extracted all the details of nearby places, including hospitals, recreational areas, restaurants, and grocery malls, using the Google Maps API and saved this information into Firebase.

articleTitle: Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis for Mobile App Review Using Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Word2Vec
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electrical, Electronics and System Engineering (ICEESE)
abstract: The proliferation of mobile applications in today’s digital environment has revolutionized the way people interact with technology, their experiences are often reflected in reviews, providing a rich source of data for analysis. Therefore, it is important to analyze the sentiment of user reviews. However, sentiment analysis can only determine whether a review tends to be positive or negative without understanding the sentiment-related aspects of the review. Therefore, further analysis is needed to extract the aspects and sentiments expressed in the reviews. Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis (ABSA) focuses on identifying aspects of entities in text and related sentiments and requires expanding features capable of representing relationships between words. Word2Vec, an alternative feature algorithm, takes a more nuanced approach by capturing the semantic relationships between words in user reviews. This research proposes a new method that combines Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Word2Vec to perform ABSA. The proposed method is used to analyze user reviews of the “MyPertamina” mobile application because the application was developed recently and is prone to instability and errors, causing commotion and concern among users. Therefore, this provides a suitable opportunity to utilize user reviews on the application to evaluate the proposed algorithm for performing ABSA. The sentiments considered in this study were only positive and negative. Meanwhile, the aspects considered are based on general user complaints which in this research are categorized as bugs, subsidies, and payments. Aspect Classification Modeling obtained an accuracy value of 71%. The results of ABSA show varying performance in various aspects—namely Bugs, Subsidies, and Payments, namely 88.3%, 73%, and 66.8%.

articleTitle: Application of Artificial Neural Networks for Performance Prediction of a Large-Scale Solar Farm in Eastern Malaysia
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electrical, Electronics and System Engineering (ICEESE)

authors.preferredName: Muhammad Iffat Waiz Bin Md Mazmi

abstract: The purpose of this study is to enhance the performance analysis of a large-scale solar farm in Eastern Malaysia by employing an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) technique. We created a reliable forecast model for energy output by including crucial environmental data such as temperature, irradiance, wind speed, and humidity. Our dataset, which ranged from December 2022 to December 2023 and included 46,682 five-minute interval records, encountered issues such as missing data owing to PV module failures. We assured data integrity and dependability by doing thorough data pre-processing, such as linear interpolation and outlier management. The ANN model, which used a 15-layer structure and the Levenberg-Marquardt method, obtained low Mean Squared Error (MSE) and high regression values (R = 0.996) during the training, validation, and testing stages, exhibiting predictive accuracy. The findings demonstrate the ANN’s usefulness in capturing the underlying patterns of solar power generation, which aligns with Malaysia’s renewable energy targets and contributes to global environmental initiatives. This study emphasizes the importance of sophisticated machine learning approaches in optimizing solar farm performance and proposes a framework for continuous monitoring and control systems to ensure operational efficiency.

articleTitle: Image Classification of Graphene Oxide Thin Films’ Sheet Resistance using a Convolution Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electrical, Electronics and System Engineering (ICEESE)
abstract: This study focuses on developing a CNN model, VGG-16, to classify microscopy images of graphene oxide thin films produced by two machines; Atomizer 2 and Atomizer 3 based on the sheet resistance values. The methodology begins with preparing microscopic images of graphene oxide thin films dataset. The dataset undergoes preprocessing to enhance image quality. It is then divided into training (80%) and testing (20%) sets. Data augmentation techniques were applied to improve the model’s generalization capabilities. The core of this research involves constructing a CNN model using the VGG-16 architecture, which is trained on the preprocessed dataset. Training and validation results are obtained to assess the model’s performance. Subsequently, a separate test model evaluates the accuracy of the image classification process. The results indicate an accuracy of 76.7% for images from Atomizer 2 and 92.37% for images from Atomizer 3, demonstrating the effectiveness of the developed AI program in classifying graphene oxide thin films microscopic images based on sheet resistance values.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-based Algorithms for Malaysian Food Image Recognition and Calories Estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electrical, Electronics and System Engineering (ICEESE)
abstract: Diabetes is a prevalent health concern among Malaysian adults, with dietary intake monitoring playing a crucial role in managing the disease. Existing dietary tracking approaches often overlook the diversity of Malaysian cuisine and therefore suffer from low accuracy in recognizing and estimating portion sizes for local dishes. To address these limitations, this study employs deep learning techniques for food recognition to develop an effective calorie estimation system tailored to Malaysian food culture. The study focuses on the investigation of three distinct models which are MobileNetV2, VGG19, and ResNet-50 in accurately identifying and classifying Malaysian food items from images. At present, there is lack of food dataset images for Malaysian cuisine, which presents a significant challenge to calorie counter or food logging app developers. Thus, 20 classes of Malaysian cuisine were generated with a total of 2,076 images used in the models. We then compared the performance of the three models using accuracy, precision, recall and F1-score metrics. The MobileNetV2 model shows a promising result with an accuracy of 97.83% compared to VGG19 with 71.05% accuracy. Meanwhile ResNet-50 achieved the lowest accuracy of 18.11%. Additionally, we evaluated the performance of MobileNetV2 on larger and more diverse cuisines to measure its scalability.

articleTitle: Oralizer prototype for deaf people: project monitoring, tests and case study
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electrical, Electronics and System Engineering (ICEESE)
abstract: This research addresses the topic of inclusion with emphasis on Deaf people, exposing the concept of the application of engineering systems through the design of a voice graphing software developed in LabView® that is used as a practice tool in the oralization process of people born Deaf but with the ability to phonate, which, according to global data, places them at a social, cultural, labor and economic disadvantage. This tool works as a technological support parallel to the therapeutic process carried out by specialists, aiming to provide support that encourages the practice of vocalization and oralization using the software presented in this article. The results collected in this work are the product of a multidisciplinary research that began in 2019, which continues in a complementary process of testing and adjustments according to the observations of users and speech therapists. It is these people together who provide feedback on the design with the aim of obtaining a functional application that seeks to irrigate Technology Applied to Inclusion and Bioinformatics in Educational Institutions and in society in general. The efforts of this research contribute to objectives 3 and 10 of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, relating to Health and Well-being and Reduction of Inequalities.

articleTitle: Electroencephalographic Biomarkers for Major Depressive Disorder and Alcohol Use Disorder
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electrical, Electronics and System Engineering (ICEESE)
abstract: Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) and Alcohol Use Disorder (AUD) are common neurological disorders that significantly impact physical health, family life, and work. Accurate diagnosis is essential for early intervention and treatment. However, conventional DSM-based diagnosis is subjective and susceptible to errors due to patient dishonesty or memory lapses. This study introduces a more reliable and objective diagnostic approach using effective connectivity (EC) from EEG recordings of 30 healthy controls, 30 MDD, and 30 AUD patients. EC, calculated via partial directed coherence, was used as input for an SVM model, achieving a peak classification accuracy of 95.3%, with perfect accuracy in the beta and gamma rhythms. These findings underscore EC’s potential as biomarkers for more accurate diagnosis and early intervention in neurological disorders.

articleTitle: Effective Connectivity of EEG Signals in Diagnosing Alcohol Use Disorder: A Machine Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electrical, Electronics and System Engineering (ICEESE)
abstract: Alcohol consumption significantly impacts public health. Excessive drinking harms physical and emotional well-being, lifestyle, and social behavior, and chronic abuse alters brain structure, leading to Alcohol Use Disorder (AUD). AUD, characterized by persistent drinking and poor impulse control, is associated with neurotransmitter and metabolic changes in the brain. Diagnosis is based on DSM-5 criteria and subjective methods like surveys and psychiatric examinations, but EEG can help predict relapse and treatment effectiveness. This study aims to develop a precise method for detecting AUD using Directed Transfer Function (DTF) and Partial Directed Coherence (PDC) algorithms as input to machine learning model. The EEG dataset comprises 30 AUD and 30 healthy control subjects. The study evaluates the accuracy, sensitivity, and precision of the algorithms, with preprocessing of EEG signals from 19 channels and analysis using DTF and PDC. The data are transformed into 19×19 adjacency matrices across 64 frequency bands. The PDC method achieved higher accuracy (94.5%) compared to DTF (89.8%).

articleTitle: Advanced Web Optimization: Leveraging Neural Collaborative Filtering and Prefetching for Enhanced User Responsiveness
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electrical, Electronics and System Engineering (ICEESE)
abstract: The continuous development of Internet technology has led to the widespread adoption of web applications, which are now indispensable in daily life. Users demand responsive websites and cannot afford long loading times. This research employs neural collaborative filtering to predict users’ next web pages and uses prefetching to improve loading speeds. An English learning website and the MovieLens 1M dataset were used for training, evaluation and testing. Results show that NeuMF, combining Generalized Matrix Factorisation (GMF) and Multi-layer Perceptron, significantly enhances web page response speeds through predictive prefetching.
